title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — Rom 5:12 'in whom all sinned' marks innate evil / all made corrupt through Adam
pass_a_gloss: Tip from the same Clavis on Rom 5:12: 'in whom all sinned' signifies not an action but an innate and essential evil lot—namely that through Adam all have been made corrupt. Tip before the aptitudo examples, Sohnius, and Zanchius on peccare actu.
pass_b_english: And again, Romans 5: as through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men, in whom all sinned. It signifies not an action but rather a habitual, or innate and essential, evil lot: namely that through Adam all have been made corrupt, etc.
source_text: Et rursus, Romanorum quinto: sicut per unum hominem peccatum in mundum introiit, & per peccatum mors, & ita in omnes homines mors pervasit, in quo omnes peccaverunt: non actionem sed potius habituale, aut sortem innatum & essentiale malum significat, quod nempe per Adamum omnes facti sint corrupti &c.

choices.choice: Rom 5:12 innate evil / all corrupt through Adam
